title: Heuristic Fallback Orchestrator — idea log
content:
Topline goal: build a lightweight orchestrator that picks fallback strategies (model variant, quantized candidate, cached response, trimmed context) per request using cheap heuristics + confidence signals. Motivation: avoid blanket fallbacks that either blow cost or degrade UX; instead make per-request tradeoff decisions to meet latency/cost/quality SLOs.

Notes / rough approach:
- Input signals: request latency budget, user tier, prompt length, cached prefix hit, recent failure rate for primary model, eval-derived quality delta between primary and fallback.
- Decision outputs: route to primary, route to cheaper quantized model, serve cached prefix+recompute suffix, do partial response (shorter reply), or respond with soft-degradation message.
- Heuristics (initial):
  * If latency_budget < 200ms and primary P50 > 180ms -> prefer 8-bit quantized model with proven quality delta < 3% on similar prompts.
  * If cached_prefix_hit and expected recompute_tokens < 40 -> serve cached prefix + live suffix.
  * If recent error rate > 5% and user is enterprise -> retry primary once then fallback to canary model.
  * If user_tier == free and estimated token cost > threshold -> suggest short-form alternative (nudge in UI).

User stories (examples):
- As a product engineer, I want a per-request decision log so I can debug why a fallback happened. Acceptance: request decision id + chosen strategy recorded and exported to console.
- As an SRE, I want emergency global disable toggle to force primary-only for incident debug.
- As a platform owner, I want to encode cost budget per org so aggregator disables expensive fallbacks when budget low.

Prototype plan (3 sprints):
- Sprint 0: simple rule engine service (stateless), expose /decide endpoint. Integrate with trace headers. Wire a config blob with rules.
- Sprint 1: collect telemetry, add confidence scoring (cheap classifier using embedding similarity to eval set), basic dashboard.
- Sprint 2: A/B rollout, canary rules, allow per-tenant overrides and policy persistence.

Open questions / risks:
- Where to evaluate model quality delta cheaply? Precomputed per-pattern eval matrix vs on-the-fly sampling? (prefer precompute offline but storage overhead).
- How to avoid oscillation when fallback causes different load patterns? Need smoothing and cooldown windows.
- Security/privacy: decision logs may contain prompt hashes; store only anonymized fingerprints.
- Interactions with rollouts: orchestrator must respect pinned versions and tenant isolation.

Metrics to track:
- %requests with fallback, per-tenant and global
- latency percentiles (P50/P95) before/after fallback decision
- quality regressions vs baseline on sampled prompts
- cost delta (tokens * model-cost) attributable to decisions

Quick config sketch (pseudo-DSL):
- rule "low-latency-quantize": when latency_budget < 200 and primary_p50 > 180 -> action: route_quantized(model_family="gpt-medium-q8", max_quality_drop_pct=3) cooldown=30s
- rule "cache-serve": when cached_prefix_hit and recompute_tokens < 50 -> action: serve_cached_prefix

TODOs (near term):
- sync with runtime team about fast routing hooks (low overhead) — @Kai
- prepare small eval set to measure per-model quality deltas on common prompt archetypes
- draft console UX for per-request decision detail (where to surface)

Notes to self: keep the initial system intentionally small: rule engine + light scoring. Avoid trying to replace full policy service (future). Use logs to iteratively refine rules.

Last quick thought: this orchestrator could double as a cost-savings advisor — generate automatic suggestions for tenants (e.g., recommend quantized variant for 12% of traffic) and surface potential savings in Console.
